notes.title: Improvements on the Horizon!
notes.notes:
[h1][i]FORTUNE SMILES UPON YOU![/i][/h1]
[hr][/hr]
[i]A stagnant sea is a dead one. Alas, worry not, the Maelstrom waters remain ever-flowing and ripe with robust violence! The winds of change bring more than just salt-stung eyes - the team works with their every breath, and today they announce these major updates coming soon.[/i]

[h1]Hot Fix Breakdown[/h1]
[list]
[*] [b]Matchmaking Improvements:[/b] We’ve optimized matchmaking to significantly reduce wait times and improve synchronization of players within the same power pool. We have fully rebuilt the source code to make matchmaking move quickly and more efficiently. Teams will now be better aligned with matching power levels for a more balanced experience.
[*] [b]Boat Shake Fix:[/b] The boat shake issue caused by Dwarves and Orcs has been addressed. While it may still occur in rare edge cases, it will now correct itself within 1-2 seconds.
[/list]
[h1]UPCOMING UPDATES[/h1]

[h2]Serpent’s Rest (NEW Map!)[/h2]
What was once the lair of the Vile Serpent, a terror to all misfortunate sailors, is now nothing more than the beast’s watery tomb. The serpentine monstrosity is believed to have perished mysteriously during The Great Sundering. But the true danger lies within the heart of these putrid waters: a colossal maelstrom, a vortex of destruction.


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32270695/58aa44cbc3da3a08a8c5d6010075374743928468.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32270695/8e2621dee2da59061f9ad098def0dba5fca47eb1.png[/img]

[h2]The Dockyard[/h2]
The docks are ready! You’ll find your entire fleet on full display in all their splendor.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32270695/13736f587fb9bfd6126b488ea5ef03729a7843b4.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32270695/cdaf3765665d9edc6e469e7b59e8f771449346c6.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32270695/75e9718b37da1581e39303b1a64894f2a8207031.png[/img]
[b]Note:[/b] some elements are still subject to change.

[h2]From the Ashes![/h2]
The Phoenix Empire rises, born anew and prepared to reduce all in their path to ash. The Phoenix Empire has new remastered boats as well as new skins coming soon!



[h2]Grand Battles on the Horizon![/h2]

You’ve come to wage war, and it’s war you shall wage. The choice of how is now yours to make.

The new Custom Lobby allows for you to create epic 15-player matches, with up to 5 teams of 3 players each. Gather your friends and jump into the action, where you can team up with full squads or even mix things up with bots for a dynamic experience. Not only that, but we’ve added the ability for two players to spectate the battles live – giving you the perfect opportunity to watch the chaos unfold without directly participating.

You can choose the map you want to play on, including some of our most popular old seasonal maps, bringing a whole new layer of strategy and nostalgia to your custom matches. The possibilities are endless, rally your crew, and sail to battle!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32270695/bdb6e6f22a78fd3ee6442dd575d2aa0e49f01944.png[/img]

[h2]Improving the Voyage[/h2]
The journey ahead bears fruit! We’ve swabbed the deck and I think you’ll find an air of clarity as you make your way around. Once more the call to battle returns and there’s loot to be had! Take part as we celebrate an eastern moon along with ships of glinting treasure.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32270695/5e67391fab695c90c9cba94a0487d1a81ce0bfbe.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32270695/836154ae9a7b8e1990305e2332bad4c00a1408e0.png[/img]

[b]Two new battle passes are on the way:[/b] the Free and Premium Battle Passes, featuring exciting themes like Treasures and Lunar New Year! [i]Fear not![/i] Existing battle passes will still be available and you can continue working to complete them!

[h1]Charting the Course Ahead[/h1]
The shipwrights at Maelstrom conjure much below the decks, for now, take heed of what’s to come...

[b]Some of the new updates include:[/b]
[list]
[*] [b]Sail in style![/b] New store to purchase new cosmetic items and skins.
[*] [b]Bigger treasure needs a bigger net![/b] New pickup ranges for all boats.
[*] [b](Pre)set sail![/b] Save multiple captain, crew, and equipment loadouts per boat.
[*] [b]Bigger booty ([i]no really[/i])![/b] Pickups for boons and treasure are larger and easier to identify.
[*] [b]Quests are back in a revamped HUD![/b] New player HUD with a larger focus on gameplay space.
[*] [b]Even keel![/b] Rebalanced values for Undead boats (e.g. [i]armor[/i] versus [i]hull[/i]) with new turning speeds and radii.
[/list]
[hr][/hr]
[i]And there you have it. Whether you be warmongers or seafarers, a cheers in your name. There will be more, in time, but until then…the blue wastes await.[/i]

[b]- The Old Mariner[/b]

~~~

Keep sending us your reports—we appreciate and are always reading your feedback!

[b]Until Next Time,[/b]
The Maelstrom Community Team

notes.title: Tidings of Treasure and Turmoil: Winter Update!
notes.notes:
[h1]Gather 'round the Captain’s Table![/h1]
Pull up a chair, warm your hands, and let me spin you a tale of the latest tidings from the high seas. Fortune favors you, for the holiday update has arrived! From decks dressed in festive finery to a brand-new tropical haven and some nasty goblin mischief, there’s plenty to keep even the saltiest sea dog entertained this season. As they say, the devil’s in the details—let’s dive in.

[h2]The Seas Don Their Holiday Best[/h2]
The chill in the air is sharp, but the spirit of the season warms even the coldest waters. The seas are dressed for the occasion, with snow falling gently on the decks, twinkling lights in every corner, and cheerful snowmen keeping watch. Trees adorned with ribbons and finery dot the horizons, adding a festive sparkle to your adventures. Whether you’re plundering or celebrating, there’s no mistaking the festive magic in the air.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32270695/9758995731adf07c0b5b0f5b7ac096b679276943.png[/img]

[h2]A Paradise Beyond the Waves (NEW Map!)[/h2]
If the frost has you yearning for warmer shores, rejoice! The tides have unveiled a vibrant NEW tropical haven—crystal-clear waters, lush greenery, and terrain ripe for exploration and conquest. But beware, Captain, this paradise won’t be yours alone. Others will be drawn to its treasures, eager to stake their claim. The question is, will you prevail?

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32270695/bf32c9d7c2ac00f178b7c5e31b1a01ffbd94c521.png[/img]

[h2]Beware the Bombers![/h2]
Trouble brews on the horizon. Those goblins, cunning and relentless as ever, have unleashed a NEW menace upon the seas. Goblin Bombers—small but deadly—have joined the fray, adapting their PvE tricks for PvP battles. These explosive pests will test your tactics and shake your resolve. Watch your stern, or it might be the last thing you see.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32270695/9621fa9152a105308e7a1f654dc79d068b7a56a9.png[/img]

[h2]Outfit Your Fleet with Festive Flair[/h2]
A fine ship should look the part, and this season, there’s no finer way to make your mark. Some NEW holiday-themed skins have surfaced, adorned in festive finery. Take it, and let the seas know who commands their waves.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32270695/1c2149048f2ad3e7313b5c0c7f1aaa1abf9f4fcc.png[/img]

[h2]Charting the Course Ahead[/h2]
The horizon holds promise, and the crew has grand plans for what’s to come. Stay vigilant for upcoming announcements and surprises—there’s plenty in store!

For now, we raise a toast to you, brave Stormers. Your passion and determination keep this world spinning, and it’s a privilege to have you aboard.

Keep sending us your reports—we appreciate and are always reading your feedback!

Until next time,
The Maelstrom Community Team.

Forthright Entertainment is thrilled to announce that it will be taking over the development and future of the critically acclaimed naval combat game, Maelstrom, from Gunpowder Games. This new chapter for Maelstrom promises to bring exciting updates and fresh content, as Forthright Entertainment focuses on enhancing the gameplay experience and expanding the game’s reach. As part of this transition, Forthright Entertainment will introduce additional content and a new season pass in the coming months, ensuring that players have even more to look forward to in the world of Maelstrom. The new content will bring fresh challenges, rewards, and gameplay mechanics, keeping the experience engaging and dynamic for both new and returning players.
We are happy to introduce our development partner on the project, the Tideturners team. 
A fresh squad of industry vets from various companies. Between them, they’ve helped bring some of your favorite games to life—Halo, Fortnite, League of Legends, Marvel’s Midnight Suns, and Rocket League. They have even been part of creating real-world experiences like Super Nintendo World. Now, they’re coming together to create something even bigger! We are thrilled to be partnering with Tideturners on reviving Maelstrom and breathing new life into the game.

As part of the announcement Forthright will be hosting an AMA live on Steam hosted from ‘Permanent Vacation’ in Florida to chat with the community.

notes.title: Development Update
notes.notes:
[Undertow Release Delayed]
Due to various circumstances, we sadly have to delay the release of the final Undead ship, which was originally expected to release in April.

We like to make sure we get things right before we release it and there are some things we need to work on before it is ready for release.

We do not have an estimated time at the moment, but will communicate that as soon as a date becomes available.

Note that development of cosmetic content for BP3 continues as expected and is unaffected.

~

In the meantime, we'd like to provide some information regarding a few big features we have been working on.

[Adventure Mode]

Adventure Mode is a brand new game mode designed for co-operative play.

In Adventure Mode, players will take their ships into a series of Encounters with escalating difficulty. The farther the team makes it, the better the rewards.

Encounters will come in various types, challenging players in a myriad of ways - from time-based trials to escort missions.  Difficulty selection and optional objectives allow players to choose their own level of challenge.

In between Encounters, players will also have the opportunity to select powerful abilities - these abilities do not persist beyond that session but will be essential to defeating encounters at higher difficulties.

Examples of Abilities:
- Mine Eater: Mines repair this ship instead of dealing damage to it and no longer apply knockback to this ship.
- Miracle: Gain a small chance to deal 9999 damage on a cannonball hit.
- Cannons Everywhere: All ships reload 20% faster (including enemies)!

Rewards earned in this mode will be treated the same as rewards earned in PvP - the same ship and mates can be used in both modes interchangeably, but of course, some builds will be more effective in one arena than the other.

[Captain Leveling: Talent Trees]

In addition to Adventure Mode, we are also working on Captain Leveling.

Players will earn items that they can give to Captains - which in turn levels them up.

Captains will earn Talent Points as they level up, allowing them to train and invest points into Talent.

Talents will either provide a passive benefit or augment the active ability of the Captain.

Example of Captain Talents:
- Morrigan: On activation, apply the ability's damage and Burning effect near the ship 
- Anvil: Torpedos can critical hit using the ship's base chance / base chance x2 / base chance x3
- Splint: (Passive) Combat speed penalty reduced by 25 / 50 / 100%
- Morte: (Passive) Siphon effect increased by 50 / 100% vs Blinded targets

Once a Talent Level has been researched, it can be assigned Talent Points. 

Talent Point assignments can be reset and reassigned at any time, however, training costs are non-refundable.

This system is expected to add a lot of customization options and change the way the game plays on both the PvP side as well as the coming PvE side.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32270695/636f1f649c13b413166069d49994d502b39f2da0.png[/img]

[h2]Welcome to Season 2[/h2]
Season 2 brings all new exciting content to Maelstrom.  Headlining this Season is the release of the Undead Fleet beginning with the sloop Wraith and her Captain. 

Season 2 is expected to run through the end of April.

[h2]New Ship: Undead Wraith[/h2]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32270695/d9dd1c9d703ca8c54060090510019b8f4ff723b7.gif[/img]
Wraith has some of the highest base top speed and turn rate in the game, rivaling Cinder and Cleaver respectively, though a lower than average deceleration means gives the ship a floaty feeling and requires more accurate maneuvering. 

The Undead sloop has no frontal cannons, but features a robust 10 cannons on both sides as well as the aft.  The addition of a large number of aft cannons significantly impacts the strategic options available to a Wraith player compared to existing ships where the rear is often the most vulnerable point on a ship.

[h3]Undead Passive[/h3]
[i]Siphon:[/i] Undead ships have lower Armor values, but compensate by using a siphon effect where their armor repairs automatically by dealing cannon damage. This means extended engagements tend to favor the Undead.

[h3]Ship Passive[/h3]
[i]Ghostly: When damaged by enemy ships, Wraith turns ephemeral for a short duration and projectiles pass through it harmlessly![/i]

This passive enables Wraith to play more aggressively or successfully get away without taking damage.  It can also allow allies to attack enemy ships without fear of friendly fire.

[h3]Ship Tier X[/h3]
[i]Phantom Push: Cannonballs knock ships back. Critical hits increase knockback force.[/i]

Phantom Push amplifies Wraith's natural evasiveness, allowing her to control enemy positioning when firing. In particular, ample rear cannons means chasing down Wraith is a difficult task.

[h2]New Captain: Merriden ‘Windreaper’ Harrowfel[/h2]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32270695/b907eb3103bb2fdb4065bef07fcb2eb2ea685f47.png[/img]

[i]Merriden 'Windreaper' Harrowfel is the daughter of Axton Harrowfel. A shade of who she once was, now twisted and delighting in the power granted her in undeath.[/i]

She has the ability ‘Darkest Door’. This ability allows players to teleport forward after a brief charge time. This ability can be used in Dead Waters or even while being boarded!

[h2]Wraith Bundle[/h2]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32270695/534949d24404382af82a65ccd0426a94005f346d.png[/img]

[h3]Upgrade Your Fleet[/h3]
Upgrade your fleet with the ghostly Undead sloop Wraith and her crafty Captain Merriden Windreaper Harrowfel.

[h3]Bundle Contents[/h3][list][*]Undead Sloop: 'Wraith'
[*]Undead Captain: 'Merriden Windreaper Harrowfel'
[*]3 Undead Mates
[*]'Nocturne' Skin[/list]

This bundle is available for 25% off for $14.99 (this is a limited time price!).

https://store.steampowered.com/app/1227510

The ship is also unlockable in the game for 1000 Gunpowder.

[h2]New Battle Pass[/h2]
A brand new Battle Pass is now available complete with new cosmetics, titles, and other goodies.

[h2]Leaderboards[/h2]
Leaderboards have arrived!  Placing on the Leaderboards will reward both a Medal as well as other prizes.  They will reset weekly and provide prizes automatically.

[h2]Legendary Mate of the Month: February[/h2]

The Legendary Mate of the Month for February is a new Legendary Shipwright for all races, including Undead.

For now, it can be earned exclusively via the new Mates of Legend quest.  

Please note that last month's new Legendary Powder Monkey has now been added to the existing Legendary Mate Contracts.

[h2]New Traits[/h2]
New Traits (both regular and legendary) are being added.

The following Traits will be added:

[quote][h3][b]Normal Traits[/b][/h3]
[h3]Guarded[/h3]
[i]+10% Armor Resistance while in Fog or Stealthed[/i]

[h3]Monster Hunter[/h3]
[i]+100% Damage vs NPCs and Monsters[/i]

[h3]Lurker[/h3]
[i]+50% Cannon Range and -25% Top Speed while in Fog or Stealthed[/i]

[h3]Disruption[/h3]
[i]When ramming an enemy ship, that ship has -50 Hull/Armor/Sail Repair for 5 seconds[/i]

[h3]Rudder Crusher[/h3]

[/quote]

[h2]Bug Fixes and Other Changes[/h2]
- ESC key can now be used to close windows and pop-ups while still continuing to function as Quit if you are already on the Ship Screen
- Corrected an issue with some Captain's abilities that could cause them to be unusable during a match
- Numerous typos/fixes have been corrected in tooltips and wiki pages
- Minor fixes to the stats of some mates (no stat changes, only incorrectly implemented or bugged stats)
- Corrected an issue that could cause an engine crash at the end of matches

[h2]More to Come[/h2]
During Season 2, we will be releasing additional content and features.  Look forward in particular to the release of the remaining Undead Ships and Captains, as well as features such as Steam Achievements.

We are also working on other exciting things (things that many players have asked for) that we'll share in more detail as they are closer to completion.

notes.title: Naval battle royale Maelstrom goes free-to-play
notes.notes:
Remember Maelstrom, the last-ship-standing game of naval combat that entered Early Access last year? The one where you can be captain of an orc ship pulled by giant sharks, and the shrinking battle-royale circle is a section of Dead Water hiding a colossal sea monster that will just straight-up eat you?

Back when it cost $20, our own Christopher Livingston said, "The toughest part of Maelstrom, from what I've played, has been getting a full match." When you could get a match it was pretty fun swinging around whirlpools launching broadsides at your enemies, and going free-to-play will presumably give player numbers a bump.

"All gameplay and progress can be unlocked by playing the game for free", say developers Gunpowder Games. "No additional purchases are needed to enjoy the game to its fullest extent. There are no ways to purchase a competitive advantage in game."

You can however buy boosts to accelerate progression, and of course there's a variety of cosmetics and a battle pass in the store. "There are no loot boxes", they add. "All Items are directly purchasable in the store."

Those who bought the game during Early Access receive a bunch of freebies, including all ships, the seasonal battle pass, 10,000 gunpowder (that's the premium currency), and a bunch of mates and exclusive stuff. 

There's a roadmap too, which notes that an undead fleet and a duel mode are on the way. Maelstrom's available on Steam.

First & foremost a giant THANK YOU for your faith & sticking with us while we’ve continued to improve the game during Early Access. It was a solid success & allowed us to get to the next leg of our journey.

The big news is that Maelstrom is becoming a Free to Play game. 

Being a premium 20$ title in Early Access worked, but moving forward as a multiplayer only title, transitioning to F2P allows a much larger player base. We expect it to bring in many new players that normally wouldn’t get a chance to sink you.

[h1]FREE-TO-PLAY DEFINITION FOR MAELSTROM[/h1]
As Free-to-Play definitions vary with games we want to define it clearly so players know what they can expect:
[list]
[*] All gameplay and progress can be unlocked by playing the game for free. No additional purchases are needed to enjoy the game to its fullest extent.
[*] There are no ways to purchase a competitive advantage in game.
[*] Players must play the game to progress & become more powerful. There are no ways to purchase a top tier ship with a powerful crew, it must be earned by playing the game. Players can however, accelerate progression with boosts.
[*] Gold is in-game currency and earned by playing the game.
[*] Gunpowder is premium currency & the only item sold for cash in-game. It is used to buy all of the premium items in the store such as the battle pass, cosmetics, boosters & bundles.
[*] Gunpowder can also be earned for free via the Battle Pass, completing quests & checking the store.
[*] Battle Passes unlock cosmetics, gold or gunpowder & there is a premium track that unlocks additional rewards for gunpowder.

notes.title: Development Update: Visuals and Quality of Life
notes.notes:
In this update, we will talk about various qualify of life things we have been working on.


[h1]Combat Feedback[/h1]

One of the primary feedback we have on our combat system from new users has been that sometimes it feels like they aren't doing damage even when they land hits. 

After investigating this issue and talking with players we concluded that the issue is one of combat feedback. Specifically, the armor mechanic can make it seem like your shots are just being nullified without any effect. 

To mitigate this, we have made some improvements to our combat feedback.

First, we have improved the visibility of the armor bars as well as incorporating an animation and sound effect related to the armor bar.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/32270695/6689009ac6f585c5ecd7416e309edad742ba82a8.png[/img]

Second, we have added icons to the scrolling combat text (SCT) to indicate what type of damage is being dealt. You can also consolidate the SCT to reduce clutter.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/32270695/089204a30a4af711aa5071ee0b8253789a1f48c6.png[/img]

Another area we have worked on is Stealth and Fog.

We have improved the visual of the fog banks and added an "edge" that appears when you are inside of them so you know exactly where you can sail and still remain hidden.

Additionally, we have added a visual effect on your ship that indicates that you are "stealthed."  This effect will be re-used in other instances when your ship becomes stealthed.

notes.title: Development Update: Quests and Medals
notes.notes:
This week we’ll talk about Quests and Medals.

But first, some answers to questions we had on last week's update!

[h1]Will mates still have random names?[/h1]
Mates will now have specific names and mates with the same name will always feature the same stat progression.  You can expect to see 2 to 4 different mates of each type.

[h1]Will mates of the same type have the same stats if they are the same level?[/h1]
Mates with the same name and type will always have the same stats if they are the same level. However, they may have a different set of trait and set bonuses as those are assigned randomly. Two Gunners with different names will have different stat progression at each level, but are intended to be comparable in power.

[h1]Are mercenaries just better mates?[/h1]
No, they are intended to offer additional choices by offering unusual stat combinations, but in terms of net benefit they are not intended to replace regular mates.

[h1]QUESTS[/h1]
The goal of our Quest system is to both reward players for playing the game while also encouraging exploration.

Each player will have 3 Standard Quest slots. 

Standard Quests come in 2 types: Competitive and Participation.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/32270695/f416e5b51586b73dea7e5f023d659714d93532d1.jpg[/img]

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/32270695/49fa3d245ac77635715e9480f17bec67909d7590.jpg[/img]

Competitive quests are just as they sound - they require to be competitive in order to compete.  If you do well, they’ll be faster to complete than Participation quests, but progress is not a sure thing.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/32270695/45307ef174cddfc100a6e1b034bbcaa7a8b08138.jpg[/img]

Participation quests, on the other hand, largely reward you for simply playing the game - and progress is generally easier to achieve though will still require you to complete specific tasks.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/32270695/cc71e9f6380b8cba69810a0e717e0e988e1f753c.jpg[/img]

In addition to the 3 slots, there will also be a bonus Daily Quest which simply requires the completion of 3 quests. This Daily Quest will refresh daily, providing a baseline of daily rewards that all players can reasonably achieve. Note that this refresh only occurs if the Daily Quest has been completed - thus if you only complete 2 quests one day, your progression is not erased.

Standard Quests can also be dismissed to obtain a new one if you do not wish to complete it.  There will be a cooldown timer to limit how often you can dismiss quests.


[h1]EPIC QUESTS[/h1]
We also have the concept of Epic Quests. All players will have the same Epic Quest during a specific duration. 

Epic Quests are intended to be completed over the course of multiple weeks, rather than over a few games. Each will consist of multiple objectives with their own rewards, along with a final reward for completing all objectives.

Epic Quests will contain a variety of reward types, but specifically will be one of the primary ways of earning Mercenaries.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/32270695/3aa222ca491a549df514cfc11943a71b6577bc15.jpg[/img]

[h1]MEDALS[/h1]
Medals, unlike Quests, are always able to be earned assuming you meet the objective. 

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/32270695/cf69e8c68bfa0f65e455bf50530374885b51969f.png[/img]

Medals are intended to reward epic gameplay moments and is not something you should expect to earn on a regular basis.  Here are some examples:
[list]
[*] Bounty Hunter III: Collect at least 9 bounties
[*] Turn the Tide: Sink the boarding ship while being boarded with 0 crew
[*] No Quarter: Sink the last 5 enemy ships and win
[*] Brave: Ram an enemy ship and sink it to win the match
[*] Swirly: Sink an enemy ship by causing them to sink in a Maelstrom
[/list]

Medals will provide some Experience when earned (we will explain the use of Experience in a later update), but primarily they are about commemorating a special moment or a special game.

A tally of all Medals earned for each ship will be kept and showcased in a Player Profile along with other fun stats.

notes.title: Development Progress Update: Release Window and Mates
notes.notes:
Hello everyone,

First and foremost, thanks for the patience. It’s been a very long time since we’ve made any announcements and we’re sorry we've been so quiet. Many conversations, a lot of work and changes have been taking place. We’re finally ready to make some important announcements about the future direction of Maelstrom.


[h1]RELEASE WINDOW[/h1]
The first thing is that we have a release window of Summer 2019. We don’t have a precise date but will update as we get closer. 

Since we have a lot to talk about we will do it in different updates over the coming weeks. Each week, we will provide details on a particular feature or system.

We will also be providing an updated roadmap soon.


[h1]MATES[/h1]
This week’s topic is MATES!

Mates are currently heavily RNG based, and while the system works quite well for the first couple weeks of play, there are a few problems with it:
[list]
[*] The RNG nature means that players do not feel a good sense of progression. After a player obtains a few good mates, it becomes much harder to make any real progress and interest can wane.
[*] Some players get 5 Star mates early, others play for a hundred hours and do not get any at all.
[*] Players are incentivized to use their best mates, rather than being able to experiment with different builds.
[*] Players end up with dozens of useless mates.
[/list]


[h1]INTRODUCING MATE LEVELING[/h1]
Upon release, the mates themselves will be functionally similar, however, how you earn them, and what you do after you have them will be different.

The earning rates for mates will be reduced. Players will no longer get mates constantly - instead, earning mates will be more rare. However, players will be able to level up mates by using GOLD. Leveling mates will increase their stats - similar to if you had obtained them at a higher level in the first place.

This will directly reduce the number of mates you get, but make the mates you own much more meaningful.  When you find a mate with a combination of stats you want to try out, you can level them up to do so instead of hoping for a higher level version of them to drop.


[h1]OBTAINING MATES[/h1]
You will still have the opportunity to find mates that are higher level right off the bat, though they will be rarer. Mates are still found in Chests which determine the level of the mate choices inside. 

Chest will also have an automatic chance to upgrade to the next level. 

For example, if you earn a Level 1 Mate Chest, all mates inside will be Level 1, but if you are lucky, it can get upgraded to a Level 2 Mate Chest, which means all the mates inside will be Level 2. Or you might get really lucky and it upgrades again to a Level 3 Mate Chest, and so on. The likelihood of it leveling up to Level 5 will be low, but it can technically happen.


[h1]TRAITS AND SET BONUSES[/h1]
We are also expanding on Mates with some new features.  We wanted to give mates more personality and interest beyond just providing static stats, and, so mates themselves are also getting an upgrade at Level 4 and 5.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/32270695/8096a8e71305739dd3e27a65c22f093a873e1e7e.png[/img]

When a mate reaches Level 4, they will unlock a new ability called a Trait.

Traits are situational abilities that apply or trigger only during certain situations.

When a mate reaches Level 5, they will unlock another new ability called a Set Bonus (we will probably give it a cooler name before launch).

Set Bonuses will be similar to existing passive and Tier X ship abilities, and are active if all 3 mates you have equipped have the same Set Bonus.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/32270695/9dbe0216272dc15d5fbe8ea08adace0ce8df2ece.png[/img]

You will also be able to reroll these traits and set bonuses if you do not like the ones the Mate came with.

The combination of these two additional characteristics will both enhance the strategic and gameplay implications of mates as well as make earning mates interesting for a longer period of time.  

We will launch with a good number of Traits and Set Bonuses to start, and we plan to add more in the future, opening up new possibilities and giving you new content to chase.


[h1]MERCENARIES[/h1]
We are also introducing the concept of Mercenaries.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/32270695/f43730dd7818f3ef52da4e7bc447588610ece083.png[/img]

Mercenaries will level up the same way as regular mates, and have access to Traits and Set Bonuses, and they won’t be stronger than regular mates.  So what makes them different then?
[list]
[*] Mercenaries will be usable for any race. They will still have a type such as Gunner, but you will be able to use them on a ship of any race.
[*] Mercenaries will have stat amounts and combinations not normally available to normal Mates - for example, you might see a Gunner that reduces Reload Time. 
[*] Mercenaries will have access to stats currently not available to Mates.
[*] Mercenaries may also come with some negative stats in order to balance out their unique array of stats - for example, a Mercenary Shipwright that gives you more Hull than a Normal Shipwright may reduce your ship’s Top Speed as a result.
[*] Unlike regular mates, the Traits and Set Bonuses on Mercenaries are available right from the start.
[/list]

Typically, Mercenaries will only be available to be earned in limited windows. We plan to have a few Mercenaries you can earn at any point in time, and while it’s possible for them to re-appear at a later date, if you really want one of them it’s best to earn it while it’s there.

~

That’s it for this week’s update. 

We’re very excited about these upcoming changes and we hope you are as well. We welcome any and all feedback and constructive criticism. 

Next time, we’ll go in depth regarding Quests. Look forward to it!

Sincerely,
Your Maelstrom team

notes.title: Summer Development Update
notes.notes:
It’s time for a Maelstrom update!

[h1]WHAT’S NEXT?[/h1]
To begin, let’s talk about short-term stuff that’s coming in the next patches or two.

The gameplay has proven out and having that base established means we can add more layers on top of it to make matches more engaging and less predictable.

[b]EMERGENT SYSTEMS[/b]
One of the biggest pieces that we’re working on is what we call “Emergent Systems.” We want to make each match played feel more unique and dynamic by introducing variable elements that impact the map and the way it’s played when they show up. We’re currently finishing the first batch of these systems:

For example there’s a storm mechanic that will cause brooding storm clouds to appear over time, making the sea much choppier and reducing sightlines. Another is Maelstroms now begin at different locations throughout the map instead of it being just a static element. Currents have also been touched and now have varying paths, and directions. There are also invasion events that may occur during matches, more on those later.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/32270695/b9012f5514a6e36406b7748ce2068c75a94c0e80.jpg[/img]

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/32270695/7f1fbc0ffe2092351855af9ad50a136a74d05104.jpg[/img]

[b]BRINEMAW[/b]
We recently reworked Brinemaw’s AI and he now patrols the waters, but we want him to do more. We’ve added a new attack where Brinemaw will pick up a nearby ship and literally bite it in half. We are also upgrading the AI so that we have more levers to adjust when and how he decides to attack players. These upgrades also lay the foundation for the new sea monster we’re adding in the near future. 

[b]DEAD WATERS[/b]
The Dead Waters mechanic is also getting an overhaul. It will now close in a circular pattern, which should provide a more predictable and more consistent experience in the end-game and avoiding the strange shapes that sometimes occur now. We are also playing with different display options for the mechanic on the minimap, as we know that some players have a hard time seeing when/where the Dead Waters are occuring.

[b]MATES[/b]
We are also in the middle of a Mates review, focusing particularly on Defensive Mates. We know that some Mate types are much more useful than other and want to increase the variety and options that player have.



[h1]LOOKING AHEAD[/h1]
In the longer term, we have a lot of exciting stuff.  It’d be too much to go through everything now, but here are some highlights:

[b]GAMEPLAY[/b]
We’ve mentioned some examples of some Emergent Systems stuff that we are already working on, but we have a lot of more of these planned and hope you will have fun discovering and seeing them for yourselves in game!  Look for things like dynamic weather effects such as lightning strikes, water spouts, as well as more involved things such as NPC Treasure fleets.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/32270695/487a9873fab0f267522b0f6d075ae9254f8a64e3.jpg[/img]

We are also working on new Sea Monsters to cause further mayhem.

[b]SHIP CUSTOMIZATION[/b]
One of the most requested features by players is the ability to customize ships. We are doing it!  We won’t give too much away, but in addition to ship skins, look forward to decals, adornments, and more fanfare that occurs when you sink an enemy ship! Oh, and lifeboats with cannons and taunts, because who doesn’t want to be able to fire offal and curse at the gloating sea-flea that sunk your ship and sailed off with all those hard earned boons?

[b]MEDALS[/b]
We have also been working on a Medal system designed to give reward players with shiny things to show off when players achieve cool/epic moments during matches.

Examples:
[list]
    [*]Tenacious: Sink the last 5 enemy ships and win
    [*]Double Strike: Sink 2 enemy ships with the same volley
    [*]Opportunistic: Sink an enemy ship by causing them in fall into the Maelstrom
[/list]

[b]EVENTS[/b]
We will also be introducing Events. These will be limited time Quests with their own reward tables for completing the objectives. 

Example:
Bourgan the Dwarven Merchant loves trout above all other food, and will handsomely reward anyone who collects enough trout for him.

Trout will randomly spawn on the maps during matches. Collect them by sailing to them. Be careful, however, as all other players will be competing for the same fish!

Rewards
[list]
    [*]Collect 50 Fish for the Title, “The Fisherman”
    [*]Collect 200 Fish for the Lifeboat Skin: “Dwarven Fishing Boat”
    [*]Collect 500 Fish for the Unique 5-Star Mate: “Bourgan”
[/list]

[b]EPIC QUESTS[/b]
For those who love the chase, we have designed Epic Quests. These will be a sequence of increasingly more difficult tasks that lead to an exclusive reward. More details to come.


[h1]THANK YOU[/h1]
Finally, we want to thank every one of you that’s shown us love and support as we grow Maelstrom and march it towards full release. There’s lots of fun to come and we’re so glad you’re on board for the ride!

Your Maelstrom team <3

Maelstrom is far from perfect but has progressed dramatically in just a few weeks and we are well over halfway to our first stretch goal! 

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/32270695/5fa1fb6315d7045af0d89fe74bf6023079c9c4ad.png[/img]

The core features have been proven, and now it's time for us to dig in to add more content, features and polish. We are now in position to take Maelstrom to the next level, and that's exactly what we're going to do.

Finally, a special thanks to everyone for the support. Your participation in discussions and feedback is invaluable. We are also grateful to the wonderful streaming community who have been showcasing our game on a daily basis. It’s really amazing!

notes.title: It's battle royale at sea in fantasy naval combat game Maelstrom
notes.notes:
Maybe it's that I kinda miss Sea of Thieves—despite enjoying it I haven't made time to play since the first week of its release—but anything with ships, sails, cannons, and sea monsters will draw my eye these days. Maelstrom, now in Early Access, has all of those, plus it's a battle royale game. Fifteen ships enter, one ship leaves.

I can't say Maelstrom takes place on the open sea: at times it feels like there's precious little room to maneuver in this ocean filled with jagged rocks and towering islands that both provide cover and damage your ship if you collide with them. And naturally, more and more of the map is being closed off as you fight. As players are eliminated, dead seas encroach and push the remaining ships together in the center of the map. It's not just a forcefield this time: the dead seas signal the approach of sea monsters who will rise from the blackening waters and smash your ship into splinters. This isn't a battle royale game where you can hide outside the safe zone and apply bandages to win.

There are three races in Maelstrom: human, dwarf, and orc, and each race has three different ships to choose from. Each ship has different perks and drawbacks: one might have better armor but slower speed and less maneuverability. A dwarven steamship I'm fond of doesn't just have cannons along the side but also at bow and stern, allowing you to fire in every direction—though in much smaller volleys than other ships. It all depends on how you want to approach combat: decide if you want to be better at long-range attacks rather than close-up combat, choose between being fleet and nimble or something more like a floating tank. You pick one ship as your first vessel, and can buy the rest later as you accumulate gold from playing matches.

Cannons aren't the only way to damage enemy ships. You can ram them as well, and certain ships are built more for ramming than anything else. You can also board other ships, sort of: pull up alongside another ship and activate the boarding attack, and you'll throw grappling hooks over, latch onto the enemy hull, and your tiny, unseen crew will do some damage before the attack expires. There are also special abilities you can earn: the only one I've gotten so far is a fireball that explodes from my bow, sweeping across the water and doing damage to anyone in its path.

It's a fun and fast-paced game as you swivel around to unleash broadside attacks, try to stay out of the line of fire as your cannons are reloaded, grab currents to speed yourself up and dart between the islands, and race to collect the floating goodies dropped when another ship is taken out. 

As you play and earn gold—there are NPC ships floating around the arena that you can sink and plunder—you also progress. As you level up you can add shipmates that give you faster sails, quicker repair abilities, and other bonuses. This means you might wind up facing ships that have better cannons than yours, improved hulls, and special attacks you haven't unlocked yet yourself, something I hope is taken into account via matchmaking. It's one thing to reach the end of a battle royale match and find yourself outgunned, but it's something else to be at a severe disadvantage right at the start.

Maelstrom is a nice-looking game built in Unreal 4, with pleasing effects and sounds, and lots of enjoyable details in the world and ship design (orc ships, amusingly, are pulled by two armored sharks). I only wish there was a bit more elegance to it: your hull integrity is displayed as a big, chunky white grid around your ship, and a massive indicator shaped like a trident extends into the water to let you know when you can fire. It's helpful that these elements are so easy to see, so you're never confused about your ship's health and capabilities, but it detracts from the art and design for these indicators to be so overbearing.

The toughest part of Maelstrom, from what I've played, has been getting a full match. Several times I've spent long minutes cruising around the lobby with three or four other players, ramming and bombing each other while we waited for more to show up, only to eventually quit because they never did. A successful battle royale game needs a solid playerbase so matches can begin quickly, and with a progression system it's doubly important to ensure players can find appropriate opponents. Maelstrom doesn't appear to have drawn much of a crowd, at least at this stage of Early Access. Here's hoping that changes soon, otherwise it might just sink.

notes.title: Patch Notes for April 25th 2018
notes.notes:
Hi everyone!  

This patch updates a variety of items, including chat options, stability fixes, balance adjustments and more!

As always, we will be monitoring the game closely and any related feedback you have.

[h1]CHAT[/h1]
- Chat can be hidden in game (go to options>online menu)
- Players can now mute & unmute players in global chat and in game by typing /mute , /unmute then selecting the name. More chat moderation tools coming online soon.

[h1]ANONYMITY OPTIONS[/h1]
- Players can choose to not spawn before match begins, this gives a degree of anonymity if desired
- Player names can now be hidden while in the matchmaking lobby

[h1]RAMMING[/h1]
- Ships engaged in offensive boarding actions can no longer ram the ship they're boarding (this typically happens with fore boarding). This has the added effect of better accuracy on ship angles and catching a ship in it's blind spot to avoid enemy cannon fire
- Rammee stun duration reduced from 1.5 to .25, this will allow the rammee to accelerate and regain some intitative after being rammed
- Damage values for low speed ramming reduced across all ships
- Head on ramming with NPC's knockback reduced
- Dwarven inability to reverse after hitting terrain fixed
- Dwarven Surgeon's Crew Health now works properly

[h1]BOARDING[/h1]
- Improved combat math for boarding actions and crew vs no crew which results in less outrageous boarding damage values
- Ships with less than min crews suffer a reload and accuracy penalty to cannons up to 50%. (at 0 crew)

[h1]HUMAN[/h1]
- Ashborne's Expanded Cabins now gains additional stat +30% hull hp
- Fury's Hold passive firing delay decreased from 1.5 to 1 & cannonball velocity bonus from 25% to 30%
- Fury's Hold's Longshot Deck removed max speed penalty, velocity from 20% to 10%, range from 20% to 15%

[h1]ORC[/h1]
- Cleaver and Bloodfin's Sawtooth cannons reload from 6 to 7
- Gorger min effective crew requirement lowered from 125 to 95. (buff)
- Gorger gains +3 fore cannons, +2 cannons per side
- Grinner's Chow Time crew and havoc bonus from 100% to 50%. Corrected tooltip

[h1]DWARF[/h1]
- Tidebreaker's base armor and hull hp reduced.
- Tidebreaker's Synched Gunports firing delay reduction from -40% to -25%
- Tidebreaker and Thunderhead's Coiled Loader Engine turn rate penalty from -20% to -10%
- Thunderhead's Granitehull Plating armor bonus and speed penalty reduced

[h1]OTHER[/h1]
- Thrasher accuracy improved
- 'Dismiss' vernacular altered to 'Discharge' on mate selection and turned red.
- Players spawning into active games shouldn't occur anymore
- Underwater rocks causing collision fixed
- Mythical floating lantern has been removed from maps (or has it..?)
- General map performance improvements
- Player's arrow on the minimap is white (in both solo and duo)
- Left Alt no longer toggles player names and armor bars
- Matches now fill up to max with players
- Player limit is now 13 in solo queue and 14 in duo queue to allow for players to have a bit more room
- Players that leave before the battle starts no longer show on scoreboard
- Player ships no longer carry 1000 gold before the battle starts. This was not exploitable, but it was confusing to see 750 loot upon leaving and not getting any
- Numerous server stability improvements (crash fixes)
- Training mission crash fixed related to physics
- Dead waters readability improved in the Maelstrom
- Buffs and booty should no longer go inside terrain geometry

notes.title: Our First Dev Update!
notes.notes:
After some hiccups at launch, it’s been mostly smooth sailing on the Abyssal Ocean - except for the warships and sea monsters at least…
But we’ve been hard at work behind the scenes!

[h1]Matchmaking[/h1]
To improve the overall experience (particularly for new players) we have tweaked the matchmaker so it distinguishes new ‘guppies’ and the experienced ‘sharks’. When possible, guppies will be matched with other guppies, and sharks with sharks. We also reduced the minimum players for a game to five, in response to player feedback!

[h1]Bug Fixes[/h1]
We had some problems with our server provider and properly resetting player data from the beta tests. Luckily that has been straightened out so that everyone can play without worrying about losing their progress. There were also a few gameplay issues that we’ve already fixed. The most notable probably being a bug with the new map which caused every player to be given Cinder, regardless of the ship they chose. It did make for some memorable scenes though before we quickly fixed it…

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/32270695/40311f9171e9b24b145559f55927b8e5270234af.jpg[/img]
[i]Cinder mayhem![/i]

[h1]Player Number Stretch Goals[/h1]

[i]A great screenshot by player CueZero.[/i]

[h1]Feedback and shoutouts are great![/h1]
Thanks so much to everyone who has left a Steam review, helped us spread the word on social media, made videos, or streamed Maelstrom. It makes a huge difference, and it’s great for our morale as well.

We want to start collecting player feedback right away! We’d love to hear from you on our Steam [url=https://steamcommunity.com/app/764050/discussions/2/]suggestions sub-forum[/url] or our [url=https://discordapp.com/invite/gunpowdergames]Discord channel[/url]!

notes.title: Fantasy naval combat game Maelstrom is coming to Early Access in April
notes.notes:
Maelstrom is a game of "fantasy naval combat" set on an inundated world where land is at a premium and wars are fought constantly to control what little dry territory remains. In case that's not bad enough on its own, what lurks beneath the waves is even worse: Monstrous creatures, larger than the biggest ships, hunt the treacherous "Dead Waters," waiting to destroy any who cross their path.   

At first glance, Maelstrom sounds quite a bit like Sea of Thieves, but it's a faster-paced game, with ships controlled by single players rather than crews. Developer Gunpowder Games described it as kind of a cross between Sid Meier's Pirates! and the Man o' War tabletop game. The Orcs, Dwarves, and Humans will each bring unique abilities and tactics to the fight—Orcs are "brutal boarders," while Dwarven ships are slow but incredibly tough—but gameplay is more arcade-style than simulation, with "an emphasis on action and moment-to-moment choices."   

Maelstrom is on Kickstarter but the campaign is actually wrapping up instead of just beginning, and it's already achieved its $10,000 goal. That's a relatively tiny slice of a development budget, but the studio said the primary goal of the campaign is to help build a community around the game. 

"Maelstrom will launch on Early Access regardless of the funding goal but we're really behind on our community building," the studio said. "The Kickstarter is meant to help us connect with genuinely interested players, willing to back the product and help build the game with us before we launch on Early Access." 

The Kickstarter campaign says Maelstrom will be focused on multiplayer, but four-player co-op is on tap as a stretch goal at $30,000 and a full-on single-player campaign at $100,000. That's an awfully distant goal—the campaign is currently sitting at a little over $11,000 in funding, with five days to go—but never say never and all that. The Maelstrom Kickstarter ends on March 27, and will likely hit at least one stretch goal before it's all over, while the Early Access launch on Steam will follow on April 11.
